To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a light scalar dark matter candidate, with a Higgs portal interaction and a mass in the range of 5-10 GeV, can explain both the CoGeNT and the annual modulation signal of DAMA.

(1) the light scalar WIMP through Higgs portal can be a candidate for the observed dark matter, with the correct relic abundance and the correct direct detection rate to explain the DAMA and CoGeNT experiments; (2) this model is testable at colliders, and at the indirect detection experiments; (3) the current Fermi LAT data on dwarf spheroidal galaxies exclude this scenario, but the data are still consistent with the CoGeNT and the DAMA results.

a light scalar WIMP interacting with the Higgs field is an intriguing possibility, and that it is worth considering the possibility that the CoGeNT and (possibly) DAMA experiments are indeed observing a light scalar WIMPs.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no compelling evidence that the DAMA/LIBRA annual modulation signal is due to a WIMP dark matter candidate.

, while the CoGeNT data are compatible with the scalar singlet DM, they are also consistent with a variety of other interpretations, including the standard model WIMP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, if the DM is a scalar particle interacting with the Higgs through the Higgs Portal, the model is in excellent agreement with all the data from DAMA, CoGeNT, Fermi-LAT and Xenon10 (2010).

we have shown that a light scalar dark matter candidate with the right mass to explain DAMA/LIBRA and CoGeNT data can be consistent with the relic density and the direct detection constraints, provided that it is coupled to the Higgs bosons.
the light scalar WIMP through Higgs portal and the CoGeNT data can be well explained by our model.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the scalar singlet model can be made to fit the DAMA and CoGeNT data with a light DM particle, while at the same time being consistent with the observed relic density, with the current constraints from direct detection, and with indirect detection experiments.
, in the absence of direct evidence of a light DM particle, the only way to discriminate among the different scenarios is to rely on astrophysical and cosmological data.
